messages:
maria: Heads-up — we just landed a support case where a customer migrated from Hosted -> Private and saw subtle policy/route differences around model pinning + KMS key rotation. They hit silent 403s on some endpoints and our fallbacks kicked to an older quantized variant. Not great.
jake: ugh. can you paste the payload they used and the control plane logs? sounds like capability negotiation failed during the handshake.
maria: payload snippet from customer (sanitized): `{"model":"redwood-v2","version_lock":true,"kms_key":"arn:aws:kms:acct:key/abc"}`. Control plane showed: `capabilities: ["generation","embeddings"]` — no `key_rotation`/`kms_bind` capability.
kai: that means the Private control plane we deployed didn't advertise the KMS binding capability. contract mismatch. we need a clear rule: clients must verify capability set before assuming semantics like version_lock + kms_key.
sam: agreed. we should add a lightweight /runtime/capabilities endpoint on the runtime agent that returns an explicit capability set + semantic version. clients call it during client init and before rollouts.
rachel: +1. also need deterministic fallback policy. if runtime doesn't support `kms_bind`, then transaction should fail fast rather than falling back to another model variant. silent fallback is a reliability/consistency bug.
jake: proposal: capability tuple: `{"name":"kms_bind","semver":"1.0.0","constraints":["aws","gcp"],"notes":"supports key rotation webhook v2"}`. if missing and request includes kms_key, return 422 with guidance link to migration doc.
maria: can we also include `compat_warnings` in the handshake so the control plane can surface during deployment? e.g., `compat_warnings: ["quantization-incompatible"]` so deploy UI warns.
kai: yes — add `compat_warnings` + `fk_handshake_id` so we can trace which deploy/request pair caused a mismatch. also include `supported_fallbacks` list.
sam: operational question — what about existing canaries? we need a migration path that doesn't break live customers. maybe a staged reject: for a month return 422 with header `x-deprecation-warning` then switch to hard reject.
rachel: good plan. make sure billing and logging mark these as security-sensitive so SRE can escalate if noise spikes.
deploy-bot: canary rolled out to infra-prod with feature flag `runtime-capabilities-v1` (build 2026.03.20-2) :rocket:
maria: I'll draft an RFC with the proposed /runtime/capabilities response shape, the client-side check, and the rollout timeline. tagging @jake and @kai for API review.
jake: tiny nit — put the semver as `capability_version` and include `behavior_on_missing` enum (`fail_fast`,`warn_then_fallback`,`silent_fallback`) so it's machine-readable.
maria: noted. I'll include example error payloads and the suggested UI copy for deploy warnings.
rachel: when the RFC is up, let's also add an integration test that simulates Private without kms_bind and asserts 422 rather than fallback.
maria: thanks all — will post RFC in #architecture later today. :thumbsup:
